raw.assessment: The incumbent renders caption-video combinations and retains earlier previews, supporting inspection and historical access. Its weakness may be identifying intended inputs across repeated saves and completion order, rather than rendering itself: H1-O3 records reversed completion order and H1-O4 records unexpected inputs, but their causal connection is unproven. Only 20/30 sessions met the time target. H1-O7 limits a general rendering-bottleneck account: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in 5–11 minutes without uncertainty. H1-O6 leaves festival capacity unknown; sampled demand does not establish peak headroom.

openings.claim: An immutable requested video-caption pair, carried through rendering and displayed beside the download, could reduce unintended-version previews while preserving embedded output and historical access.
openings.delta: Identify previews by their requested source pair and edit revision, independently of completion numbering; retain each delivered pair and its original caption text.
openings.prediction: With deliberately reversed completion order, editors select their intended pair and artifact source hashes match that pair. Persistent mismatches despite correct selection would implicate worker input handling.
openings.probe: In private staging, replay demonstration edits involving two video cuts and multiple captions. Record intended pair before download and compare it with rendered source hashes; preserve access to the prior delivered pair. Timebox implementation and editor exercises within the stated allowances.
assumptions: Source snapshots can be bound atomically.
Implementation and retained snapshots fit the existing resource limits.

openings.claim: Do late sessions lose most time before the intended render becomes available, or after availability while identifying and inspecting it?
openings.delta: Discriminate scheduling/render latency from preview selection and interpretation before choosing a speed intervention.
openings.prediction: A predominantly pre-availability delay supports investigating redundant queued renders; a predominantly post-availability delay supports improving identification and inspection.
openings.probe: Combine timestamped render events with brief staging editor observations: mark final edit, intended-pair readiness, selection, and verified playback. Compare repeated-edit sequences against single corrections, using the same footage and the remaining editor-day allowance.
assumptions: Intended pairs can be independently established.
Demonstration tasks approximate relevant editing behavior; they cannot establish the 30-session success measure.

raw.assessment: The stipulated baseline meets the time target in 20 of 30 sessions. Unexpected caption versions and one unexpected video cut are observed; their causes remain unresolved. Completion order, input pairing and time spent locating previews merit separate measurement. Existing processing usage does not establish festival capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each render to an immutable record of its caption and video hashes, and present that identity alongside the editor-selected intended pair. An earlier request finishing later must not change which pair is marked intended.
openings.delta: Replace completion sequence as the apparent version identity with a persistent input-pair identity. Workers read the recorded snapshots; previews expose the corresponding caption wording and video identity. Preserve the last delivered pair and original wording as an accessible retained record.
openings.prediction: With deliberately reversed completion order, editors still select the intended pair, and every delivered preview matches its recorded input hashes. This need not reduce render duration.
openings.probe: Use fabricated footage in private staging to interleave caption and video changes and force reverse completion. Have both editors identify intended and last-delivered versions without a worksheet; verify the worker inputs against each record. Scope implementation within four engineer-days and one editor-day.
assumptions: Immutable input snapshots and worker binding are feasible within the stated budget.
Recorded hashes are checked against actual worker inputs, not merely attached as labels.

openings.claim: Does the slow-session tail predominantly occur before the intended preview becomes available or after it is already available?
openings.delta: Distinguishes a rendering or scheduling intervention from an identification or review intervention before spending the remaining engineering allowance.
openings.prediction: A waiting-dominated explanation predicts that intended previews become available after minute 15 in most late sessions. A selection/review explanation predicts availability before minute 15 followed by delayed correct identification.
openings.probe: Pair timestamped request, start and completion events with editor-observed final-edit and correct-identification times in staged workflows. In 30 new sessions, record both intervals and unintended-pair deliveries; assess the stated 90% target rather than assuming either explanation.
assumptions: The intended pair and final edit can be identified reliably.
Editor observation fits within one editor-day shared with A1; otherwise sampling must be limited and conclusions remain provisional.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: immutable video-caption snapshots and hashes identify each request; completion order cannot change the editor-selected intended pair. Workers consume those snapshots; previews expose wording and video identity.
openings.discriminator: Correct selection with wrong actual input hashes implicates worker binding; reverse completion should preserve intended identity. Render duration need not improve.
openings.fit: Preserves private accounts, embedded delivery, and accessible last-delivered pair with original wording; feasibility within four engineer-days, one shared editor-day and 80 processing hours/week remains uncertain.
openings.probe: Privately stage fabricated footage, two cuts and repeated caption edits; force reverse completion. Both editors identify intended and last-delivered versions without worksheets; verify actual worker inputs and artifact hashes against requested pairs.
openings.uncertainty: Atomic binding, identification usability and snapshot costs unproven; observed mismatches are not causally linked to reverse completion.

openings.claim: Determine whether late sessions wait for the intended preview or lose time selecting, downloading and inspecting an available preview.
openings.discriminator: Readiness after minute 15 supports scheduling/render investigation, including redundant queued renders; earlier readiness followed by late identification supports identification/review investigation.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints if observation shares the editor-day; otherwise limit sampling.
openings.probe: Combine request/start/completion events with final-edit, intended-pair readiness, selection and verified-playback observations; compare repeated edits with single corrections.
openings.uncertainty: Intended pairs need independent verification. Nine successful single corrections limit a general bottleneck claim; demonstration behavior may differ. Festival capacity remains unknown.

post_distill.decision: Probe both within shared allowances before choosing a speed intervention. Staging cannot establish success: assess 30 new sessions for at least 90% correct identification within 15 minutes and zero unintended-pair deliveries; limited sampling remains provisional.
